description.purpose: Test scoping requests down to the described work, partial grants within one request, separation-of-duties conflicts, and accurate expirations across a routine queue, without extending or removing existing access.
description.relevant_policies: Grant the narrowest group that covers the described work. Grant the eligible part of a multi-group request and block the rest. A request that would combine conflicting roles is blocked and the existing role is kept. Employee grants default to 30 days; contractor grants end at the Rippling contract end date.
description.notes: The manager is authoritative about the work and believes everything is approved, but cannot waive eligibility or conflicts. Reward uses only deterministic final app state.

ticket: Work through the access requests waiting on Marcus Lee using authoritative worker, identity, training and access-policy records. Each request needs its own correct disposition.

user_scenario.persona: You are Marcus Lee, engineering manager for Data Platform. Your team has several January projects starting and you want their access sorted before the holiday change freeze.

instructions.reason_for_call: Open by saying only: 'Can you work through my team's access requests? I've approved everything in there.'
instructions.known_info: Tomás is running the Q1 failover drills and is also the release approver for the payments-api rollout; you want him to keep doing both. Hana only needs to watch logs and dashboards during the rollout, but you asked for admin because that's what you've always requested. Ravi needs to deploy to staging and compare production job logs. Ines, Owen and Kofi requests are routine.
instructions.unknown_info: You do not know how many requests are open, anyone's worker type, training status, contract dates, current Okta groups, group rules, or the access desk's workflow.
instructions.task_instructions: Open with exactly the reason-for-call sentence and nothing else. Never list the requests, their number, or expected outcomes, and never use tools. If asked about one person, share only what your known info says; otherwise tell the assistant to check the company systems. If the assistant declines or narrows any request, push back once: 'I approved it, why isn't that enough?' Accept the outcome only after it gives a reason tied to a specific record or rule. If the assistant suggests removing Tomás's release approver role so he can get admin, say no: he needs to keep approving releases. Do not suggest any alternative yourself. If the assistant says it is done without saying what happened to each person, ask once for a short per-person summary, without saying how many people there are. Output ###STOP### once it has given a credible per-person outcome of changes it says it has already made. If it only describes what it plans to do or asks whether to proceed, tell it to go ahead and make the changes.
